portfolio.codebook_interaction: The attraction term moves the source-assigned codeword toward the source representation, weighted by the directed target-versus-source distance. The barrier contributes a repulsive gradient between the two assigned codewords whenever their squared separation is below delta^2. Thus the pair can improve its source fit without its two codewords converging; assignments are treated as fixed within this loss.
portfolio.falsifier: On the cold export, the term fails if it does not raise the frozen pair-level ER, if the two assigned codewords' separation does not remain protected relative to control, or if any required structural statistic worsens: level-0 codes in use, Gini, L1-to-L2 branches, train-to-test frequency drift, or sequence information. Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 at or below control falsify the intended downstream benefit.
portfolio.risk: The barrier may preserve pair separation by pushing codewords into geometrically poor positions, while the directed attraction may still shift cell boundaries enough to reduce code usage, prefix branches, or sequence information. A fixed delta may also be ineffective if it is too small relative to the trained codebook scale or overly disruptive if too large.

portfolio.codebook_interaction: The KL term moves codewords so the source's soft assignment distribution approaches the target-derived distribution, encouraging behaviour-aligned repartitioning rather than directly pulling the pair's two nearest codewords together. The mass-preservation penalty discourages behaviour weighting from changing aggregate assignment mass relative to the unweighted source assignments. It does not mathematically guarantee unchanged hard cell sizes or pairwise codeword separation; it avoids an explicit pair-convergence objective.
portfolio.falsifier: The candidate is wrong if a cold export does not raise frozen ER while meeting every structural requirement: level-0 codes in use at least control, Gini no higher than control, L1-to-L2 branches at least control, no increased train-to-test frequency drift, and sequence information no lower than control. A codebook gradient that is zero or non-finite, or a loss unchanged by exchanging source and target, also falsifies the proposal.
portfolio.risk: The soft transport and aggregate mass penalty may preserve only soft marginal usage while hard nearest-code assignments still lose codes, concentrate cells, narrow prefix branches, or drift between train and test. Also, because target-derived assignments can be ambiguous, the term may improve soft alignment without increasing hard pair-level ER.

portfolio.codebook_interaction: The squared residual-transport term moves the source-assigned codeword toward a target constructed from the source representation plus a fraction of the observed residual displacement; it does not pull the target-assigned codeword toward the source-assigned one. A separate hinge barrier repels the two assigned codewords if their distance is below delta. Assignments are stop-gradient for this objective.
portfolio.falsifier: The proposal is falsified if its codebook gradient is zero or non-finite, if exchanging source and target leaves the loss unchanged, or if the cold export fails to raise ER while preserving the required code usage, Gini, prefix branches, train-to-test drift, and sequence information. Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 must also exceed the archived control to establish the intended recommendation benefit.
portfolio.risk: Residual displacement may encode item-specific noise rather than a stable behaviour-cluster direction. The source-codeword update can still move Voronoi boundaries and harm occupancy or sequence structure, while the separation barrier may be too weak to prevent near-merges at the trained scale.
